gallery.filename: Current River MO 2009-06-15 n65 below Welch Spring crop1.jpg
gallery.title: File:Current River MO 2009-06-15 n65 below Welch Spring crop1.jpg
gallery.source: Current River MO 2009-06-15 n65 below Welch Spring crop1
gallery.description: The upper Current River in the Ozarks of Shannon County in southern Missouri, between Welch Spring and Akers Ferry:  This is part of the Ozark National Scenic Riverways, a national park created by Congress in 1964 to preserve the Current and Jacks Fork Rivers.  The Current River contains the worlds largest concentration of first magnitude springs (flow greater than 100 ft3/s (3 m3/s)), making it a favorite for floating.  Welch Spring contributes an average of 121 ft3/s (3.53/s) to the flow of the river, practically doubling its size and speeding its flow.  The large amounts of cold spring water contribute to a unique environment in the river; though located in a subtropical climate, watercress and other cold water flora and fauna thrive here.
categories: Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation

gallery.title: File:Round Spring - Missouri, 16.jpg
gallery.description: Round Spring is approximately 55 feet deep, rising in a nearly circular pool of water before flowing under a natural bridge to join the Current River of the Ozark National Scenic Riverways in Missouri.  On an average day, some 26 million gallons (98 million liters) of water flow from the spring.[1]

gallery.filename: Big Spring Lodge early in the project, with windows boarded up, tarps on the roof, and construction barricades in place. (075548df-77dd-46d8-8cd8-a66c1b70ca98).jpg
gallery.title: File:Big Spring Lodge early in the project, with windows boarded up, tarps on the roof, and construction barricades in place. (075548df-77dd-46d8-8cd8-a66c1b70ca98).jpg
gallery.description:
A stone building with peaked roof and chimney covered by a construction tarp stands surrounded by forest. The windows are covered by plywood and orange construction barricades can be seen in the foreground.
Big Spring Lodge early in the project, with windows boarded up, tarps on the roof, and construction barricades in place.
Keywords: Big Spring; Big Spring Lodge

gallery.filename: A freshly stained cabin, still awaiting its restored windows. (0be6593d-e481-49f3-bd9b-6abb7c8b655e).jpg
gallery.title: File:A freshly stained cabin, still awaiting its restored windows. (0be6593d-e481-49f3-bd9b-6abb7c8b655e).jpg
gallery.description:
The left two-thirds of the frame are taken up by the dark brown stained shingled side of a single story building with a peaked roof and two square windows near the top which are covered over with unpainted plywood. A low stone retaining wall is visible parallel to the foundation of the building and turns at a right angle around the back side. In the right third of the frame, visible past the building, orange mesh construction barriers can be seen in the near distance and sparse, leafless trees can be seen further back with blue sky visible beyond them.
A freshly stained cabin, still awaiting its restored windows.
Keywords: Big Spring; Big Spring Lodge; Big Spring Cabins

gallery.filename: A door is being stripped of paint and prepared for restoration. (29c72bc8-43c9-43a3-b436-7e9265d3a786).jpg
gallery.title: File:A door is being stripped of paint and prepared for restoration. (29c72bc8-43c9-43a3-b436-7e9265d3a786).jpg
gallery.description:
An antique door lies on a support frame with the bottom towards the top of the frame and the top, which has six rectangular windows, is oriented towards the bottom. Wood grain is visible over most of the door and marks where hinges and latches have been are also visible.
A door is being stripped of paint and prepared for restoration.
Keywords: Big Spring; Big Spring Lodge

gallery.filename: A restored, stained door (left) placed next to an unrestored door for comparison. (31c3cf71-ba67-4ff8-a01b-d24ed1fc19e9).JPEG
gallery.title: File:A restored, stained door (left) placed next to an unrestored door for comparison. (31c3cf71-ba67-4ff8-a01b-d24ed1fc19e9).JPEG
gallery.description:
Two doors stand side by side, leaned against the exterior of a grey building. The one on the left has a nine frame window the fills the top third and is stained wood with a glossy finish and a beveled inset panel in the bottom third. The one on the right has a six frame window in the top third of the door and an inset panel of vertical wooden slats in the bottom third and it is made of unfinished dark wood.
A restored, stained door (left) placed next to an unrestored door for comparison.
Keywords: Big Spring; Big Spring Lodge

gallery.filename: A worker showcases sample finishes to be used on the restored doors of the lodge and cabins. (37bd90af-f728-412a-8708-93b77b685c3d).JPEG
gallery.title: File:A worker showcases sample finishes to be used on the restored doors of the lodge and cabins. (37bd90af-f728-412a-8708-93b77b685c3d).JPEG
gallery.description:
A man in a bright yellow t-shirt whose head is not visible in the frame stands behind a table and gestures with one hand towards a board that starts unpainted on the end farthest from the viewer and progresses through three shades of finish, from lighter to darker, towards the viewer. There is a darker finished section of wooden wall panel underneath the first board, and framed windows can be seen to the right of the boards. Other bits of boards with different finish are scattered around the table and a shelf with cleaning supplies can be seen in the background.
A worker showcases sample finishes to be used on the restored doors of the lodge and cabins.
Keywords: Big Spring; Big Spring Lodge
